ledger.x: c. 440: the Nalas hold Bastar and Koraput. The page dates the dynasty only to the "6th century"; the Narendrasena page puts the Nala king Bhavadattavarman at war with the Vakataka around 445, so the start is a bridge before that. Varaha-raja, known from gold coins, is…

c. 443: Bhavadattavarman takes Nandivardhana. "an invasion by the Nala king Bhavadattavarman of Bastar" that reached Vidarbha and took Nandivardhana; the Nala page: Bhavadatta extended Nala territory into Vidarbha, "possibly at the expense of the Vakatakas". The year is not given; it is bridged before the recapture.

c. 445: Narendrasena retakes Nandivardhana. "Around 445 CE, during the final years of Kumaragupta I's reign" he retook Nandivardhana, "his former capital, by driving out joint Gupta and Nala forces"; the page says he may have sacked the Nala capital, without naming it. Narendrasena's reign is c. 455-480 on the same…

c. 580: Kirtivarman I destroys the Nalas. The Kirtivarman I page gives no year for the Nala campaign (the Aihole inscription calls him "the night of doom" for the Nalas; reign 566-592); 580 is the middle of his reign, a bridge. The Nala page gives only "6th century" and a small branch that "may have ruled a small area…

wars.name: Narendrasena's war against the Nalas
wars.outcome: The Vakataka king Narendrasena retakes Nandivardhana from joint Gupta and Nala forces around 445.

certainty.note: No border is given; the Nala kingdom is Bastar and Koraput by name only.
